label: SYNTHETIC READER: a test instrument, never a reader. Fictional; not evidence about the book; not readership.
first_thing_i_would_do: Write one page of rules for a single research-and-draft agent, with the stop line first: it may gather and draft from named sources, and it must stop and ask me before anything is published.
why: The chapters give me what I judge by: the failures are named with commit ids, and the editor is the one who signs and the only one who restarts. I would buy the longer book for the register of claims and the brakes chapter. The series page tells me nothing about whether it is for newsrooms, so I would not commit to the series on that page alone.

by_section.why: The unlocked part and the conductor's honest refusal to take another lane's irreversible job are clear, and the fair-minded narrator is credible. The figure is only a brief to the designer, so I could not check the minute-by-minute claim.
by_section.quote: A rule that keeps everyone in their lane also means that when one lane is busy, the job waits.

by_section.why: This is the control I care about: anyone may stop, only the editor restarts. It is not a rubber stamp.
by_section.quote: Anyone on the team could stop everything. Only I could start it again.

by_section.why: I like that three accounts are kept with dates. But the second and third are thin, and 'the 95% was the token usage' reads as a correction without saying what the 95% was before. The editor does not choose, which leaves me unsure what to cite.
by_section.quote: I am not going to pick one for you now.

by_section.section: What did not work: the interview
by_section.why: The freeze that hid a correction is a real editorial lesson: a held story missing its late fix. Specific, sourced, transferable.
by_section.quote: when you freeze something, write down what is waiting to go in when you unfreeze it.

by_section.section: After the hold: the empty chair
by_section.why: Too short to carry its weight. It asserts that reviewers shared an identity with the people they read, but gives one example at most. For a newsroom, independent standing-apart is the whole point, so I wanted a concrete catch or miss.
by_section.quote: I would staff it first, next time.

by_section.why: Actionable: who stops, who restarts, who decides in the owner's absence. I would do it today.
by_section.quote: Until you have, nobody restarts it.

by_section.why: The team is temporary and the record is not. That is the archive-and-corrections-log idea a newsroom already understands.
by_section.quote: The team is temporary. The record is not.

by_section.why: Twelve roles in a run of one-liners; the second half of the list blurs. I wanted to know which one a newcomer starts with before reading the whole cast.
by_section.quote: Every number in this book is in my register, or it is not in this book.

by_section.section: Two scenes from the second factory
by_section.why: The best section for me. A source-checker catches the author's nicer sentence and it is corrected in the open. The failed brake on 1 November stays in.
by_section.quote: Nobody argued for keeping the nicer sentence.

by_section.why: Honestly labelled as a plan that has not run. One brief owner, one morning board, one hold: very close to a desk.
by_section.quote: Two people editing one brief is how a team ends up with two briefs.

by_section.why: Five steps with a 'what to check' under each. The shop-owner examples translate easily to a newsroom. The cost line is dated and admits that the day's own cost is not in the record.
by_section.quote: If you cannot say when it must stop, it does not have one.

by_section.why: The two lines repeat the five steps and the pointer to the longer edition, and add nothing here.

by_section.section: A book about you doing it
by_section.why: Brand and mood with no source I can check. 'Not a range of birth years' is vague, and I do not see why a writer launching a publication should care about the series.
by_section.quote: Generation ZX is not a range of birth years

best_line: Nobody argued for keeping the nicer sentence.
worst_moment: Chapter 6, the series page: 'the youngest and the most experienced side by side, as they were in the room in Faro'. It is a claim about a room that I cannot trace, and it reads as marketing after two chapters of traced failures.
cut: The chapter 5 'Do this now' and 'Zoom in' repeat the steps and the longer edition. Trim the second-factory cast list to the roles a newcomer would start with.
notes: Contradiction to check: chapter 4 says security's chair never came, and chapter 5 says this time security came. That works, but a one-line pointer in chapter 4 would help a reader who stops there. For a newsroom I would also like one concrete example of the editor's signature stopping something, since the editor's control is what I am judging. Figures are all designer briefs in this draft, so I could not judge them.
